tutorial.title: Database Setup
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to set up a database file in Express using SQLite

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's dive into how we can manage data using a separate database.js module to facilitate database interaction within our Express app.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
First, we need to set up our database. Within our database.js file, we require the better-sqlite3 module and define our database filename.

Make sure to pick require, followed by "better-sqlite3", and finally "database.db".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Set up a connection named db for the local songs.db file using the better-sqlite3 package.

Make sure to pick require, followed by "better-sqlite3", new, and finally "songs.db".

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Next, we'll set up our tables. We can use db.exec to execute the statement and use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS to create the table if needed.

Make sure to pick db followed by . and then exec, CREATE TABLE, IF NOT EXISTS.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use db.exec to execute a statement and CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS to create a table if needed.

Create songs only if it is missing, using the column definitions shown.

Make sure to pick db, followed by ., exec, CREATE TABLE, and finally IF NOT EXISTS.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Last, we export db via module.exports.

Make sure to pick module followed by . and then exports, =, db.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use module.exports to share a value with files that import this module.

Make the established db connection available to files that import database.js.

Make sure to pick module, followed by ., exports, =, and finally db.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can now import it into our JavaScript file. We will then be able to use this connection to interact with our database.

Make sure to pick require, followed by "./database.js".
lessons.hardModeContent:
In script.js, import the connection exported by the nearby database.js file and store it in db.

Make sure to pick db, followed by require, and finally "./database.js".

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's use this connection to query information from our database. Firstly, we'll prepare a statement to get information.

Make sure to pick db followed by . and then prepare, "SELECT * from songs".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Prepare, but do not run yet, a statement named getSongsQuery that selects every column from songs through db.

Make sure to pick getSongsQuery, followed by db, prepare, and finally "SELECT * FROM songs".

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
With our prepared statement, we can now execute it to get our data. We do this by calling all on our statement.

Make sure to pick getSongsQuery, followed by .all().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Run getSongsQuery to collect every matching row in songs, then print that collection.

Make sure to pick songs, followed by getSongsQuery, all, console.log, and finally songs.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statement do?

It creates a new table if it doesn't already existIt checks if the table has data before creating it

It creates a new table if it doesn't already exist.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What does the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statement do?

Decide whether this SQL statement creates songs when that table already exists.

It creates a new table if it doesn't already existIt checks if the table has data before creating itIt clears an existing table before recreating it

It creates a new table if it doesn't already exist.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a table if it doesn't already exist.

Make sure to pick CREATE followed by TABLE and then IF, NOT, EXISTS.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add the SQL clause that creates the companies table without failing when that table already exists.

Make sure to pick CREATE, followed by TABLE, IF, NOT, and finally EXISTS.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Export the created database connection via module.export.

Make sure to pick module followed by . and then exports, =, db.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Finish the line that exports this db connection for another file to require.

Make sure to pick const, followed by =, db, module, and finally exports.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is exported by this file?

The db object, which represents the connection to the SQLite databaseA function to run SQL queries directly

The db object, which represents the connection to the SQLite database.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You import this file with const connection = require("./database.js").

Which call can you make directly on connection to prepare a query?

connection.prepare("SELECT * FROM friends")connection.db.prepare("SELECT * FROM friends")connection("SELECT * FROM friends")

connection.prepare("SELECT * FROM friends").

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the imported db to prepare a SQL statement.

Make sure to pick db followed by db and then ., prepare, "SELECT * from songs".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use the imported db connection to prepare a statement called getSongsQuery that selects all columns from songs.

Make sure to pick db, followed by getSongsQuery, db, prepare, and finally "SELECT * FROM songs".

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:

lessons.hardModeContent:
What does require("./database.js") do in this file?
